page_title: HyperWrite unveils AI agent for web tasks | VentureBeat

summary.name: HyperWrite AI agent
summary.one_liner: An experimental AI personal assistant from HyperWrite (OthersideAI) that browses websites and completes tasks like a human user, accessed through a Chrome extension.
keywords: ai agent that browses the web
use_cases: automating basic web tasks such as placing an online food order
looking up addresses and filling in web forms
personal assistant for everyday online chores
exploring early AI agent browser control
summary.what_it_does: HyperWrite's experimental agent can browse the web and interact with websites much like a human user, according to a VentureBeat article. In a closed Zoom demo, it navigated to the Domino's Pizza website and began an order, looking up an address and zip code, and the demo ended before any credit card number was entered. It is accessed through HyperWrite's Chrome extension. The company said the agent would initially be enabled only for select test users. The article says the design intent is for the agent to check with the user before acting, rather than ordering without their knowledge.
notable: Operates a web browser like a human, clicking and entering information on live sites
Accessed via a Chrome extension; users request early access
Designed to check with the user before taking actions
Compared in the article with AutoGPT and BabyAGI agents
caveats: Experimental, shown only in a closed demonstration
Initially limited to select test users
Article notes human-level web skills could be misused for phishing, hacking or scams
